thread:
alex.s: Quick sync — proposing an extraction for enrichment: split a thin host-facing adapter and a reusable enrichment-core. Sharing spike results + rollout sketch for comments.

maria: sounds good. can you call out hard constraints? db semantics, 99th pctl latency, and how we keep deployability.

alex.s: constraints: 1) preserve hot-path 99th <= 250ms, 2) zero-downtime cutover with immediate rollback option, 3) avoid any write interleaving that breaks downstream consumers, 4) preserve telemetry (token cost, trace ids).

devon: adapters or sidecars? sidecar helps local cache, adapter gives clearer service boundary.

alex.s: tradeoffs: sidecar simplifies host-local caching but couples ops; adapter (separate process) gives independent scaling and clearer ownership. ops burden slightly higher.

jess: we have several sync enrichment steps relying on shared in-memory caches. plan?

alex.s: long-term: extract cache into a small managed caching service with gRPC + LRU + metrics. short-term: keep local caches in adapter and run a coherence shim until extraction.

piotr: db migrations: enrichment writes two tables; transactional expectations exist.

alex.s: migration plan: dual-write (shadow-write) to new tables, read from old until verified, then flip reads via feature flag. reconciliation job runs asynchronously for the short non-transactional window.

maria: add strict consistency verification and a throttled reconciler before switching reads. no surprises.

alex.s: agreed. rollout: canary 5% for 6h -> 25% -> 100%. monitor: error rate, 99th latency, reconciliation drift, downstream diffs.

devon: tests: contract tests for adapter-core RPCs, migration harness replaying traces, chaos tests that kill adapters mid-request, synthetic load for latency SLO.

jess: ops checklist: runbook, warm caches before cut, dashboards and alerts, rollback playbook, and cost estimate for extra capacity during migration.

piotr: SLO relaxation? we should reserve a maintenance window but prefer auto-rollback if SLOs breach.

alex.s: we'll keep production SLOs but have a communicated canary window; auto-rollback on thresholds.

release-bot: deploy-candidate created: pr/4521 contains adapter skeleton + dual-write wiring. CI: unit, integration, contract tests passed.

maria: also ensure adapter structured logs include trace-id + tenant-id top-level. lost this once and debugging took long.

alex.s: will add structured logging + token-cost tags.

devon: infra ok if adapter is small and uses existing helm charts. will require RBAC for cache service.

jess: volunteer to draft the formal RFC with timelines and reconciler algorithm?

alex.s: I will draft RFC today and link PR. tagging @maria @devon for review.

maria: I can review tomorrow morning.

piotr: I will validate migration SQL and add reconciliation queries with Pg team.

alex.s: next steps: RFC, runbook to /docs/runbooks/enrichment-modularization.md, and add canary harness to integration pipeline.
